<reason>CON made the motion easier to decide by hanging on grant-on-request plus “even if it complicates,” showing personhood cannot name the river’s interest, binds non-requesters, and delays necessary works. PRO’s standing-gap and colonial-refusal case stayed morally sharp, but after pressure it softened into joint guardianship and still had to accept sewage-plant challenges. CON’s named-plaintiff alternatives and immortal-docket weighing were the cleaner voting rule.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s Rebuttal 2: A’s two-community answer became co-management in a personhood mask, and conceding channel-altering sewage injunctions made the motion’s “even if it complicates” clause fatal.</best_rebuttal>
